articles.title: Anthropic shares fall a day after blockbuster opening
articles.summary: Other tech companies have also taken a hit as share markets broadly slump.

blocks.text: Anthropic's share price has dropped back towards its initial public offering (IPO) price a day after its soaring market debut, as the broader tech sell off continues.

The artificial intelligence (AI) company's introduction to the Nasdaq stock exchange on Thursday was a crucial test for the industry and was largely seen as a success, with trading starting at $111.50.
However, Anthropic's shares fell on Friday, dropping more than 10% to about $87.30, close to its IPO price of $83, and the broader stock market declines seen on Thursday continued.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index fell 2.8% in morning trade, the S&P 500 was down 1.2% while the Dow Jones Industrial Average remained largely flat.
The maker of the Claude chatbot raised a record $81bn in its initial public offering (IPO), but its share price moved significantly in the first day of trading.
The shares peaked at $115 on Thursday, before easing to end the day up 17% at $97.17.
Analysts said volatility was to be expected in the first days or even weeks of Anthropic's trading, as the company was the first frontier AI firm to go public so had no direct peers.

Some have also noted the similarities with Elon Musk's SpaceX, which at the time of its debut in June was the largest IPO on record. Shares in the rocket and AI company experienced large swings in its first few weeks of trading.
Ed Moya, a strategist at market intelligence firm AlphaSense, said Anthropic's blockbuster IPO did not appear to have restored confidence in the broader AI market.
While AI demand was still very strong, Moya told the BBC that investors were trying to answer the question of how much were they willing to pay for that growth.
"As we've gone through the past past few weeks, it seems that there's been more risks that have surfaced," he said.
"Right now you're starting to see Wall Street is trying to shift from rewarding growth at any price, to demanding stronger cash flow and a clearer path to profitability."

articles.title: Rodrigo Duterte camp asks ICC to reject ex-Davao City cop's prior recorded testimony
articles.summary: PRAGUE, Czech Republic - For former President Rodrigo Duterte"s defense team, the testimony of the ex-Davao City police officer sought by International Criminal Court (ICC) prosecutors to be admitted…
articles.byline: ANDY PEÑAFUERTE III, JAY-VEE MARASIGAN PANGAN

blocks.text: PRAGUE, Czech Republic – For former President Rodrigo Duterte’s defense team, the testimony of the ex-Davao City police officer sought by International Criminal Court (ICC) prosecutors to be admitted in court has “serious deficiencies” and must be rejected by Trial Chamber III.

Duterte’s counsel Peter Haynes contests the admission of P-0002’s evidence, saying the articles invoked by the Office of the Prosecutor to collect and preserve it require proof that a witness can no longer testify orally.
“Absent such proof, the prior recorded testimony cannot be admitted and the witness must be called to give his evidence viva voce,” Haynes said in a public redacted filing released on November 18.

Haynes’ legal challenge comes roughly ten days before the ICC’s trial of the former president opens, with information still unclear about which witness testimony and evidence will be admitted in court.
Haynes described P-0002 as a “central Prosecution witness” and said his testimony is the most heavily cited in the prosecution’s trial brief.

Prosecutors seek to admit P-0002’s preserved testimony under Article 69(4), following what they described as a “unique opportunity” to interview him and obtain evidence that “may not be subsequently available.”

The prosecution also informed the chamber that P-0002 is “no longer available” to testify before the court. The filing conceals the details of that significant risk, as well as the reason for P-0002’s expected absence.

The Common Legal Representatives of the Victims (CLRV) support the admission of P-0002’s evidence, which they described as having “particular importance” due to his “position and first-hand knowledge”, which makes his testimony “particularly significant” in the former president’s case.
Defense, prosecution clash over evidence
Duterte’s lawyers dispute how the prosecution obtained P-0002’s evidence, questioning whether it has adequately established its unavailability.
Aside from arguing that the prosecution has no documentary evidence to support P-0002’s evidence, Haynes also questioned the reliability of the former policeman’s account.

He pointed to alleged inconsistencies concerning charged Incident 1, including differences over the year of the incident, the number of victims, the perpetrators, and the circumstances of the killings.

In the Prosecution’s Trial Brief, Incident 1 refers to the killing of three unidentified alleged drug pushers by Davao Death Squad members in or around 2013 in San Rafael, Davao City. Prosecutors said then-Davao City Mayor Rodrigo Duterte “instructed police DDS members that there was a job to be done against three alleged drug pushers.”
The filing also said P-0002’s statement appears to be the sole source for several allegations concerning Duterte’s conduct.

These include prosecution allegations that Duterte created a police “Death Squad”, told police DDS members they were being tasked as hitmen, ordered co-perpetrator Vicente Danao “to kill three or four men”, gave financial rewards to DDS handlers, and financed weapons and ammunition through this intelligence fund.
These allegations were raised in the prosecution’s case and were not established as findings by Trial Chamber III.

Aside from this, Haynes pointed to another redacted individual or entity that he referred to as the “sole source”, which has “not provided a sworn statement” about the circumstances of P-0002 and his situation, which remains concealed.
Much of Haynes’ allegation over that “sole source” is redacted, but he cited obscure statements that he said “reveal an intention to steer the proceedings”.
“Taken together, these shortcomings undermine P-0002’s descriptions of Mr. Duterte’s alleged actions,” Haynes argued.
“Given the Prosecution’s submission that P-0002 is [REDACTED] and in the absence of any supporting documentation, the only appropriate remedy is the exclusion of his evidence.”
Corroborations in P-0002’s evidence
Among the 62,000 items of evidence prosecutors disclosed to the defense, Haynes said they found no material corroborating claims about P-0002.
The defense also said the former policeman’s statement and associate materials “portray a witness deeply hostile towards Mr. Duterte and paint a picture of an individual who is emotionally unstable.”
Describing the materials, including handwritten notes whose contents are redacted, Haynes said P-0002’s evidence “reveals a paranoia” and “leads him to exaggerate” information.
“This aligns with P-0002’s erratic conduct,” Haynes argued.

The other batches of associated material, including two handwritten notes, an unsigned and undated typed affidavit, and a Philippine National Police personal data sheet, “were not used or commented on P-0002” and had no verification or authentication.
The defense also questioned how the interview was conducted, stating that a counsel appointed by Pre-Trial Chamber I at the time represented the defense “as an observer."

Calling it a “significant error”, Haynes said the previous counsel’s involvement was “negligible” and that their presence “was a formality” that gave “no substantive protection to a future defendant’s rights”.
Criminal records of witnesses, victims sought

In a separate filing, Duterte’s lawyers asked judges to order prosecutors to seek and disclose criminal history information concerning witnesses and victims identified in the prosecution’s updated Trial Brief.
The defense wants records of arrests, convictions, sentences, non-judicial dispositions, arrest warrants and Interpol notices.
It argued that such information may be relevant to witness credibility and may also be “potentially exculpatory.”
The defense singled out P-1302, whom it identified as the first prosecution witness expected to testify.
It said open-source material indicates that P-1302 has been the subject of a redacted number of legal cases in the Philippines, but no corresponding judicial records have been disclosed.
Duterte’s lawyers also said the criminal records of alleged victims could be relevant to testing the prosecution’s case theory on police claims of self-defense.

They argued that records showing an alleged victim had an arrest warrant or faced proceedings for an offense such as illegal possession of firearms could support the legitimacy of a particular police operation.
The defense asked the Chamber to order the prosecution to immediately seek and obtain requested information.
For witnesses expected to testify before January 1, 2027, it asked that the materials be disclosed no later than November 30.
Trial Chamber III has yet to rule on either request.
Duterte’s crimes against humanity trial is scheduled to open on November 30. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: President Marcos expands school voucher program to kinder, elementary
articles.summary: President Marcos has signed a law institutionalizing government-funded vouchers for Filipino students from kindergarten to senior high school to expand access to quality private education and ease…

blocks.text: November 21, 2026 | 12:00am
Elementary students in General Trias, Cavite line up during flag ceremony in this file photo from June of this year.
Edd Gumban

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos has signed a law institutionalizing government-funded vouchers for Filipino students from kindergarten to senior high school to expand access to quality private education and ease congestion in public schools.

Signed on Nov. 12, Republic Act 12327, or the Basic Education Voucher Assistance Act, covers private basic education institutions receiving government assistance through vouchers for qualified students, teacher subsidies or other school assistance.

The law extends assistance to Filipino students from middle-middle-income households and below, with priority given to those enrolled in congested public schools, particularly in areas without nearby public schools or institutions offering subjects and electives aligned with their chosen senior high school academic tracks.
“Subject to the availability of funds, the implementation of the provisions in this Act for the kindergarten and elementary levels shall commence in school year 2027-2028,” the law stated.

The Department of Education (DepEd) welcomed the legislation, saying it would provide higher subsidies to low-income families while protecting current beneficiaries of the Educational Service Contracting Scheme and the Senior High School Voucher Program until they complete their basic education.
DepEd also said priority would be given to congested public schools, multi-shift institutions and areas lacking public school options.
“Families will be empowered through a public registry detailing nearby participating private schools, slots and fees,” the department said.

The law also establishes the Bureau of Private Education within DepEd to oversee the supervision, regulation, quality assurance and implementation of government assistance programs involving private education.
The bureau will serve as the department’s focal office for engaging private education stakeholders and supporting participating institutions.

To protect learners and ensure accountability, the law prohibits schools from withholding student records because of delayed government payments and establishes anti-fraud measures, including a centralized system for verifying learner eligibility and school compliance. It also provides whistleblower protection to encourage the reporting of irregularities.
The rules and regulations will be released within 60 days, subject to funding availability.
Funding for the law’s implementation will initially come from DepEd’s current budget and will subsequently be included in the annual General Appropriations Act.
The budget will be equitably distributed among all regions, including the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.

articles.title: Money changer exec in Martin plunder case surrenders to NBI
articles.summary: A co-accused of Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez has surrendered to authorities and was granted conditional immunity, according to the Office of the Ombudsman.

blocks.text: November 21, 2026 | 12:00am
The Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) released screenshots from CCTV footage showing former House speaker Martin Romualdez inside the detention facility.
MANILA, Philippines — A co-accused of Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez has surrendered to authorities and was granted conditional immunity, according to the Office of the Ombudsman.

The anti-graft body said Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp. president Felicito Guevarra, who is facing a P7.4-billion plunder charge over supposed kickbacks from government projects, surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation after the prosecution moved to cancel his passport.

The ombudsman granted Guevarra conditional immunity, provided that he cooperates fully and truthfully in the case, turn over all of Samchan’s records and devices, remain in the country and stay under protection of the Department of Justice.
His immunity will be revoked and his prosecution will resume should he break any of the conditions, it said.
“Mr. Guevarra personally handled Samchan’s operations. His testimony and records will help the prosecution trace the movement of funds alleged in the charge sheet,” the ombudsman said in a statement.
It said Samchan has returned to the Bureau of Treasury all its earnings from the questioned transactions. However, the ombudsman emphasized that restitution does not erase criminal liability.
It is also not the basis of the immunity granted to Guevarra.
Linked to Estrada

Meanwhile, a total of P855 million worth of projects, composed of pumping stations and street lights, are linked to detained Sen. Jinggoy Estrada, Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) engineer Carlo Rivera told the Sandiganbayan.

During the bail petition of Estrada on his plunder charge, Rivera recalled in 2024 that former Bulacan First District engineer Henry Alcantara asked him about P355 million worth of projects that could be allotted to the senator.
It was then that he asked the DPWH section chief about available projects, and he was told the P355 million could be used for pumping stations.

Rivera said Alcantara gave him a separate project list for P500 million worth of solar street light projects for the third district in Bulacan, which he forwarded to then-DPWH National Capital Region director Gerard Opulencia upon the order of Alcantara.

articles.title: President Marcos: China’s playing of ‘Anak’ a ‘gracious’ gesture
articles.summary: While the use of Freddie Aguilar’s classic hit “Anak” as musical accompaniment during his entrance to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) gala dinner last Wednesday sparked…

blocks.text: November 21, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — While the use of Freddie Aguilar’s classic hit “Anak” as musical accompaniment during his entrance to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) gala dinner last Wednesday sparked online debate, President Marcos described it as a “very gracious choice” by the Chinese.

A Chinese orchestra played “Anak” as Marcos and First Lady Liza Marcos entered the hall for the APEC dinner in Shenzhen last Thursday, before they greeted Chinese President Xi Jinping and First Lady Peng Liyuan.
In an interview in China on Friday, Marcos said the song was played during his entrance, while “Leron Leron Sinta” was also played during the dinner.

“I thought their choice of that song was again a very, very warm gesture from the Chinese to, I guess, just make you feel at home and understand that they are thinking of how to express their comity and friendship,” Marcos said.
The use of “Anak,” a song about a repentant son, prompted online discussions about whether its lyrics carried an implied message about the territorial disputes between the Philippines and China.
Some questioned whether the song’s theme was an appropriate representation of Marcos and the country.
Marcos dismissed the speculation, saying the Chinese were simply playing popular music for their guests, similar to how the Philippines welcomes foreign dignitaries with familiar songs.
“I think you’re reading too much into it. They were just playing a song for their guests, the same way that we play popular songs in our country for our guests,” he said.
Presidential Communications Office Secretary Lino Cayetano, who accompanied Marcos to China, said “Anak” was also played during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations ceremonies in Manila.

“We played it too, because some people already knew it. That is why it was a very nice choice for the Chinese to make. They chose it because it is not only famous in the Philippines but also in many other countries,” Marcos said.
“Anak,” which means “child,” was a major hit in the Philippines in the 1970s before becoming an international success. The song has been translated into 51 languages.

articles.title: Philippines, Japan sign emergency loan, water supply grant deals
articles.summary: The Philippines and Japan have signed two landmark deals that will allow loans and grants to help boost the Philippine economy and improve water supply systems in Cotabato City.

blocks.text: November 21, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines and Japan have signed two landmark deals that will allow loans and grants to help boost the Philippine economy and improve water supply systems in Cotabato City.
Both deals are expected to benefit the Philippines amid current economic challenges and water supply problems in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).

The Japanese embassy in Manila announced yesterday that Ambassador Kitagawa Katsuro and Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro signed and exchanged notes for the “Emergency Support Loan for Enhancing Economic Resilience and Poverty Alleviation” on Nov. 13 with a loan limit of approximately 70 billion yen.

“With its reliance on the Middle East for approximately 95 percent of its crude oil and petroleum products, the Philippines is significantly affected by increasing energy and raw material prices and supply chain instability stemming from the situation in the Middle East,” the embassy said.
“Rising production costs and logistical bottlenecks are posing challenges to the stable supply of products that underpin Japan’s supply chains.”

The Japanese embassy noted that under the “POWERR Asia” initiative launched by Japan, its support will bolster emergency economic measures, such as stabilizing energy supply to mitigate the impact of the situation in the Middle East and addressing soaring prices, thereby stabilizing and strengthening supply chains throughout Asia.
At the same time, such initiatives will also contribute to Japan’s economic security and benefit Japanese companies operating in the region.

Earlier on Nov. 9, Kitagawa and Lazaro also signed and exchanged notes for a project aimed to improve the water supply system in Cotabato City with a maximum grant amount of approximately 3.644 billion yen.

The embassy said the project will expand water supply facilities in Cotabato City, the capital of BARMM where socio-economic development has lagged due to prolonged conflict and limited access to safe water.
“By expanding safe water supply services, this cooperation will contribute to the consolidation of peace and development in Mindanao through the reduction of disparities.”

articles.title: Senate panel wants Bato to explain prolonged absence
articles.summary: The Senate ethics committee is set to call a hearing on the complaint filed against Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa over his prolonged absence from official duties in the chamber, committee…

blocks.text: November 21, 2026 | 12:00am
Sen. Ronald Dela Rosa talks to media at the Senate of the Philippines in Pasay, Metro Manila on May 13, 2026.
AFP / Jam Sta Rosa

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate ethics committee is set to call a hearing on the complaint filed against Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa over his prolonged absence from official duties in the chamber, committee chairman Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente Sotto III confirmed yesterday.
In an official committee document uploaded by group Wag Kang KuCorrupt, Sotto informed Dela Rosa that the complaint against him was “compliant in form and substance.”
Sotto confirmed that he sent a formal letter to Dela Rosa last Oct. 22, giving him 15 days to respond to the complaint filed by the group represented by Barry Gutierrez, Cielo Magno and others.
“Yes, that’s a letter I sent Sen. Dela Rosa,” Sotto told reporters via text message when asked to verify the document.
With the 15-day period having lapsed, Sotto noted that the committee’s schedule has been delayed by other major proceedings in the chamber.
“I will call a hearing soon. Budget and impeachment just getting in the way,” he said.
Asked whether Dela Rosa or his lawyer had submitted a reply to the notice, Sotto said he would verify the status of the submission.

According to the Oct. 22 letter signed by Sotto, the ethics panel met in an executive session on the same day and found the complaint, as supplemented, “in substantial compliance, both in form and in substance, with Section 17” of the committee rules.

Pursuant to Section 18(C) of the rules, the committee formally transmitted the complaint to Dela Rosa and invited him to provide “any information relevant to the complaint, including a written response, within fifteen (15) days from receipt of this notice.”
The complaint was originally filed on Feb. 25, 2026 and the committee informed Dela Rosa of the filing on April 28.
On May 4, the panel returned the complaint to the complainants for failure to substantially comply with Section 17 of the rules, prompting the group to file supplemental affidavits on Sept. 14.

articles.title: PAL firms up first Dreamliner order
articles.summary: Flag carrier Philippine Airlines is adding up to 20 Boeing 787-10 Dreamliners to its fleet, as it maximizes its international network for future growth.

blocks.text: November 21, 2026 | 12:00am
Planes land and take off at Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Pasay City on March 23, 2026.
STAR / Ryan Baldemor
MANILA, Philippines — Flag carrier Philippine Airlines is adding up to 20 Boeing 787-10 Dreamliners to its fleet, as it maximizes its international network for future growth.
In a signing, PAL entered into agreements with aerospace giant Boeing to buy 15 Dreamliners as was announced during the Farnborough International Airshow in July.
The agreements also cover the opportunity to purchase another five in the future, providing PAL with the flexibility to broaden its fleet as demand requires.
The 787-10, the largest member of the Dreamliner family, aims to boost PAL’s fleet upgrade. The aircraft will enable PAL to raise capacity for medium- and long-range flight.
Boeing committed to deliver the Dreamliner to PAL over the next decade. PAL will also become the first domestic carrier with a Dreamliner in its fleet, marking a new era for Philippine aviation.
PAL Holdings Inc. president and chief operating officer Lucio Tan III said the Dreamliner would enhance the airline’s fuel efficiency, given that the aircraft is equipped with new technologies.
“Its advanced technology, greater passenger capacity and improved fuel efficiency will also help us serve more passengers, improve our product offering and operate more efficiently,” Tan said.
The Dreamliner that PAL ordered would be powered by GE Aerospace’s GEnx-1B engines, one of the aviation industry’s most reliable mechanisms right now.
The Dreamliner is arguably the industry’s most popular aircraft because of its features. For one, the unit is the lightest and smoothest widebody jet, making long-range flights more comfortable.

Further, the 787-10 that PAL ordered is the biggest variant of the Dreamliner family, capable of flying between 300 and 375 passengers. The aircraft can fly as far as 13,890 kilometers and for PAL, this means reaching destinations across the Pacific Ocean.
Boeing also flexes the sustainability advantage of the Dreamliner, as it burns 25 percent less fuel compared to previous generations.
For passengers, the Dreamliner brings better comfort in its dimmable windows, higher humidity for dry air and reduced noise during turbulence.

articles.title: President Marcos, Chinese foreign minister discuss West Philippine Sea issues
articles.summary: President Marcos is hopeful for “better” and “improved” relations with China, following his recent conversation with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Shenzhen, China.

blocks.text: November 21, 2026 | 12:00am

Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. arrives in a vehicle at the Philippine International Convention Center for the opening ceremonies of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Meetings in Manila on November 15, 2026.
AFP / Rolex Dela Pena / Pool
MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos is hopeful for “better” and “improved” relations with China, following his recent conversation with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Shenzhen, China.
Marcos said while he didn’t get the chance to speak with Chinese President Xi Jinping, he had a “long conversation” with Wang on several matters, including the West Philippine Sea.

“As you can imagine, it’s very difficult to have any kind of extended interaction with President Xi, because he’s also very, very busy,” the President told the Philippine media delegation who covered his participation in the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders’ meeting and related activities yesterday.

“I had an opportunity during the gala dinner, quite by coincidence, or maybe by design, I don’t know, to sit next to Foreign Minister Wang Yi. And over dinner we had a long conversation on several matters,” he said.
According to Marcos, he discussed with Wang “how we can move together, how we can lower tensions in the West Philippine Sea, how we can deal with each other in a better way.”
Marcos said he is “very optimistic” that the Philippines and China will “find better ways to deal with the difficulties that we have.”

“I think, because Foreign Minister Wang Yi and I were able to speak, even though I wasn’t able to talk to President Xi, we were able to discuss a lot of things that I think will be for the better,” he said, emphasizing the two countries’ trade and investment relations.
China, Asean want COC – BBM
Meanwhile, Marcos said China and all member-states of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations are supportive of finalizing a code of conduct (COC) in the South China Sea.
“All the ASEAN leadership would like a COC. And I think, I feel it very strongly that China would also like to have a COC. And they say so,” Marcos said.
He credited the support and cooperation of the Chinese on the progress of finalizing the COC.

Marcos said Singapore, the next chair of the ASEAN, now holds the initiative to move things forward for the finalization of the COC, which seeks to establish rules for managing maritime disputes and preventing confrontations in the South China Sea.
“I’m highly encouraged by the attitude that they bring to those negotiations. And let’s really hope that Singapore will be able to host the actual finalization of the COC,” Marcos said.
At a press conference after the closing ceremony of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits in Pasay City on Tuesday, Marcos said the major issues surrounding the proposed rules have been settled.

articles.title: Catherine Zeta-Jones' daughter says parents warned her about 'nepo baby' label
articles.summary: Carys Douglas, 23, made her stage debut this year in Anton Chekhov's play, The Seagull, in the US.

blocks.text: Catherine Zeta-Jones's daughter has said her parents warned her people might have "preconceived notions" about her embarking on an acting career, as she shared her views on the "nepo baby" label.
Carys Douglas, 23, made her stage debut this year, playing the lead role of Nina in Anton Chekhov's The Seagull in Brooklyn, New York.

Zeta-Jones who is married to Michael Douglas, son of Hollywood star Kirk, previously said the "nepo baby" term was "horrific". It refers to children of famous parents perceived to have achieved riches and success off their parents' backs.
But the young actor said her parents taught her to build her "own identity" and that she has learned how to deal with the "pressure".
During an interview with Elle Spain, Carys Douglas said her parents "do not hide" from her that people would have preconceived ideas about her.
"They taught me that building my own identity depended on me and no one else. It was my responsibility, and it still is.
"As time has gone on, I've come to understand that there are different ways to deal with that kind of pressure," she said.
Her father, star of hit 1980s films such as Wall Street and Fatal Attraction, recently stated that he is not a fan of the "nepo baby" label, calling it an "unfortunate title".

"I guess you could say that about any business. The same thing with Hollywood royalty. My father's father was a junkman," Douglas, 82, said, referring to Kirk, who was considered a Hollywood Golden Age icon.
Zeta-Jones, 57, from Mumbles, Swansea, also criticised the phrase, saying it was "horrible because these kids didn't ask to be born into this, they're finding their own way in life".
"You have to go with your dreams, your passion," Zeta-Jones said.
She added: "But they love it, and they're good. Otherwise, Michael and I would be the first to go, 'you know what? Maybe law school looks really good'."
Zeta-Jones' big break came when she landed a West End role in 42nd Street in 1987, before she became a household name in the UK in 1991 after starring in the ITV hit The Darling Buds Of May.
She has since become a global superstar, with roles in The Mask Of Zorro, Entrapment, Traffic and 2002's adaptation of Chicago, for which she won an Oscar for Best Supporting Actress.
The couple's children, Dylan and Carys, have both followed in their footsteps into acting.
Michael Douglas said his children have been performing "since they were in kindergarten".
"Every play, every show, summer theater camps, graduating... I mean, they've done so much work. It's unbelievable," he said.
Douglas and Zeta-Jones' children predominantly grew up in the US, but the family regularly travels to Wales, a place they are fond of.
Speaking to British Vogue last November, Carys Douglas said her summers were spent reading on her grandmother's sofa and travelling around the Gower Peninsula in Swansea.
"I feel so lucky that this is where I'm from," she told the magazine, reflecting on the "weird but magical places" scattered across the peninsula.
"Those beaches are some of the most beautiful in the world," she said.
"The Gower Peninsula is breathtaking."
She also spoke about her "theatrical" family's traditions, recalling how "there'd be lots of little competitions for singing and pantomime shows all summer".
"It's true, the Welsh love to sing," she added.

articles.title: Sara Duterte impeachment trial Day 45: Cale88 seen as small-time despite millions in money flows
articles.summary: The 45th day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte began with the Senate impeachment court ordering OVP spokesperson Paolo Panelo to explain his remarks alleging bias by some…

blocks.text: The 45th day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte began with the Senate impeachment court ordering OVP spokesperson Paolo Panelo to explain his remarks alleging bias by some senator-judges.
Panelo defended his comments as part of his freedom of speech.

Defense witness and Trade and Industry Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo testified that Cale88 Foods Corp., a listed business interest of the Vice President’s husband, Manases Carpio, is a registered micro, small and medium enterprise.
Likewise, Rodolfo said the firm stopped operations in 2025 due to a change in ownership.
Rodolfo also said that, from 201 employees in 2024, the firm only had 50 workers in 2025 based on its submissions to the Board of Investments under DTI.

At the same time, Rodolfo testified that Cale88 only had zero and two employees in 2024 and 2025, respectively, based on the firm’s General Information Sheet submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission.
The witness said there was no reason for Cale88 Foods Corporation to surpass its declared sales of P208 million in 2022 to 2025.

He made the testimony after senator-judges pointed out that the money inflow and outflow to Cale88 accounts reached P1.2 billion worth of covered and suspicious transactions based on the records of the Anti-Money Laundering Council.

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said it was puzzling that Cale88 did not apply for incentives when it registered before the BOI, which regulates fiscal incentives for firms and considering the billions worth of bank transactions that it recorded under its account.
Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros said it "sounds bananas" that Cale88 was able to produce 422,000 kilos of banana chips in 2025 with only two employees and three officials.

Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Director Pilar Marilyn Pagayunan, meanwhile, testified that Cale88 Foods Corp. was granted product registration documents, or the Certificate of Product Registration.
The FDA official, however, said she won’t be able to testify on the capacity of Cale88 to produce over 400,000 kilos of banana chips.
Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero asked the defense team if they bought a sample of the banana chips.
Defense counsel Justin Gular, however, said the defense does not have samples of the chips.
Gular said they will present a proper witness who can speak on Cale88’s production.
The impeachment trial will resume on December 1 to give way to the ongoing Senate deliberations on the proposed P7.2 trillion budget for 2027.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: AFP eyes kinetic weapons to boost territorial defense
articles.summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) is eyeing the acquisition of kinetic weapon systems to strengthen the country's territorial defense and protect its sea lanes.

blocks.text: Published November 20, 2026 11:28pm
The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) is eyeing the acquisition of kinetic weapon systems to strengthen the country's territorial defense and protect its sea lanes.

In a report by Chino Gaston on "24 Oras" on Friday, US President Donald Trump announced a $2-billion military loan for the Philippines during his visit to the country, equivalent to around P127 billion.
Of this amount, $400 million will be allocated to strengthening the military's capabilities to deter potential attacks in the West Philippine Sea.
One of the capabilities being considered involves kinetic weapons, which can strike targets at long range on land or at sea.
These weapons use the kinetic energy generated by the speed and mass of a projectile, such as missiles and bullets, to hit their targets.

"These are weapon systems which have larger range. So, there are missile systems. The missile systems will not be effective if there is no radar. Of course, you need to detect where the threat is," Major General Oliver Maquiling, director of the AFP's DAGITPA Exercise, said in a mix of English and Filipino.
AFP Chief of Staff General Antonio Nafarrete said these weapons are important in deterring foreign vessels from entering the country's sea lanes.

"We concentrate now on kinetic requirements basically for territorial defense talaga, ensuring pag may mga… kasi ito archipelagic. Pumapasok na yung mga PLA (People's Liberation Army) na mga naval vessels dito sa sea lines of communication natin. That’s international kasi, so we must have that deterrent capability," Nafarette said.

(We are now focusing on kinetic requirements, primarily for territorial defense. Given that the Philippines is an archipelagic country and Chinese naval vessels are entering our sea lines of communication, we must have that deterrent capability.)
The deployment and use of missile systems are among the capabilities being tested and practiced during the AFP's AJEX DAGITPA military exercises.
The Philippines already operates several missile systems, including the BrahMos cruise missiles acquired from India, which have a reported range of up to 300 kilometers.
The country also has C-Star anti-ship cruise missiles from South Korea. —Jean Mangaluz/VBL, GMA News

articles.title: 1 in 8 Filipino students were vape users in 2024 – DOH
articles.summary: (1st UPDATE) Some users of e-cigarettes in the Philippines were only 7 years old when they started vaping, the 2024 Global Tobacco Survey finds

blocks.text: 'TOBACC-OFF'. Youth advocates against tobacco, nicotine, and vapes during the press conference announcing the 2024 Global Youth Tobacco Survey findings on November 20, 2026.
Jelo Ritzhie Mantaring/Rappler
(1st UPDATE) Some users of e-cigarettes in the Philippines were only 7 years old when they started vaping, the 2024 Global Tobacco Survey finds

items: In 2024, 12.8% of Filipino students aged 13 to 15 reported using electronic cigarettes, a decrease from 14.1% in 2019, but lifetime use increased to 26.7%.
Health officials express concern over early e-cigarette use among youth, with some starting as young as 7 years old, and emphasize the need for stricter regulations.
The Department of Health is advocating for a smoke-free and vape-free environment, with legislative efforts underway to protect public health and reduce exposure to secondhand smoke.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – One in eight Filipino students aged 13 to 15 years old were users of electronic cigarettes or vape in 2024, the Department of Health (DOH) said on Friday, November 20.
According to the DOH’s 2024 Global Youth Tobacco Survey, the rate of students who used vapes within the month they participated in the study was at 12.8%. It was a decrease from 14.1% in 2019.
But the survey also found that 26.7% of students have “used electronic cigarettes in their entire life,” slightly higher than the 24.6% in 2019.

“What we see as a potential room for us to actually act on, we can see that those who actually experiment… only half of those are actually current users of electronic cigarettes,” Dr. Alethea de Guzman, director of the DOH Epidemiology Bureau, said in a press conference.
Health Assistant Secretary Lester Tan said it was alarming that there are e-cigarette users who started at 7 years old, according to the survey.

blocks.caption: Department of Health

blocks.text: De Guzman said that smoking is the number one risk factor for non-communicable diseases.
She pointed to the accessibility of vape and to the information about these products for the apparent increase in the use of e-cigarettes.
“Are our youth being targeted by the industry, by those that are selling and distributing these products?” De Guzman said.
According to the survey, e-cigarette use is the most prevalent among Filipino youth at 12.8%, followed by cigarettes (7.1%), smokeless tobacco (5.7%), and other smoke tobacco (4.1%).
Alethea also noted that the figure of current e-cigarette users was higher than the figure for current cigarette users.

“However, this rate shows cigarette smoking persists among the youth with those age 16 years and above having around twice as higher rate at 13.1% versus the younger age group was 6.2% to 7.1%,” she said.
“The rate for current use is increasing as the students get older,” she said in a mix of English and Filipino.

Au Quilala, executive director of the Philippine Legislators’ Committee on Population and Development (PLCPD), said that while it is the responsibility of adults to prevent young ones from accessing cigarettes and vapes, it is the government’s duty to enforce existing laws.
Republic Act No. 11900 or the Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products Regulation Act provides that 18 years old is the minimum allowable age for the purchase, sale, and use of these products.
It also prohibits the sale, promotion, advertising, and product demonstration of vapes within 100 meters of the perimeter of a school, playground, or other facility frequented by minors.

“It is important that we amend RA 11900. Children should not have access to vapes. I hope we raise the minimum age to access vape or cigarette,” Rizza Duro, Philippine Smoke-Free Movement national coordinator, said in Filipino.
Exposure to secondhand smoke also increased across settings of home, enclosed public places, and outdoor places, according to the survey.
There was also high exposure to secondhand smoke in school properties in 2024, Alethea noted.

blocks.caption: Department of Health

blocks.text: Health advocates rallied for the passage of the smoke-free and vape-free environment bill, which seeks to protect public health from exposure to secondhand cigarette smoke and vape aerosol in all public spaces and workplaces, especially those frequented by children.
The proposed measure has moved forward in the House of Representatives following its approval in the chamber’s health committee on November 11, the PLCPD said.

Amid the legislative push, Dr. Dominic Maddumba, DOH Health Promotion Bureau head, said the agency had released a template ordinance for local government units to implement a smoke-free and vape-free environment.
He said the DOH is also stepping up efforts on making smoking and vaping cessation services accessible.
But they will also study the messaging against the use of vape and tobacco products as graphic pictures may have already lost their effectiveness.
Over 8,000 students across 96 schools participated in the 2024 Global Youth Tobacco Survey. The DOH presented findings coming from over 6,000 students aged 13 to 15 years old. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Measles in America: Here's a constructive approach to beating the disease, based on Brazil's experience
articles.summary: The US is now officially a measles contagion zone. By mid-2026, there were more infections than in all of the previous year. But the country could beat measles again, just like Brazil did two years…

image.caption: Brazil distributed more than 16 million doses of the measles vaccine in 2026 and maintained its measles-free status; in the US, vaccination rates have fallenImage: ZUMA Press/IMAGO

blocks.text: Health experts saw it coming — the fact that after 26 years, the US would lose its status as measles-free. Back in July 2026, DW reported how one epidemiologist had suggested an 'amnesia' about the measles risk was pushing a growth in US infections.
Four months later, it was official. On November 17, 2026, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) said the US had lost its measles elimination status, along with Mexico.
But it doesn't have to stay this way.

Look at Brazil, where in 2019, with more than 21,000 measles cases, the country also lost its measles-free status. But within five years — during the COVID-19 pandemic — it fought and won back its measles-free status. And since 2024, Brazil has stayed measles-free, even as the highly contagious disease spread across the rest of the Americas.
In 2026, with the data available up to the time of writing this article, Brazil had only had 70 measles cases. They were all linked to infections brought in from abroad, often from neighboring Peru.
Brazil has fewer people than the US, about 213 million compared to the US's nearly 350 million, but the two countries are similar in size. So the comparison is worth considering.
What Brazil does differently from the US
Brazil moves fast. The PAHO asks countries to respond within 72 hours of a suspected case. Brazil's own rule is a ladder:

items: Report cases within 24 hours
Investigate within 48 hours
Vaccinate people close to the case within 72 hours

blocks.text: It has also made hunting for cases a national habit.
In a program called "Dia S", health workers knock on doors and visit schools, daycare centers, and churches to find people who may be sick but have not seen a doctor.
Brazil holds targeted, mass vaccination days called "Dia D". There was one in November, in the area where Brazil borders Colombia and Peru.
If someone is diagnosed with measles, health workers try to track down every person the patient may have met ("contact persons") and they vaccinate them and other people living nearby.
The country has so far provided more than 16 million doses of measles vaccination in 2026 and has donated 500,000 doses to Peru.

Brazil isn't perfect, though. According to official estimates from the World Health Organization, only 76% of children got both required doses of the vaccine in 2025 — well short of the 95% target. Experts warn this leaves the country at risk because measles is so highly contagious; a country needs to be as close to 100% immunized as possible to protect people and stop the disease from spreading.
"Elimination is not a trophy that we win once and put on a shelf. It must be protected every day," says PAHO Director Jarbas Barbosa.
Is the US experiencing a vaccine crisis?
Why the US lost its measle-free status

The US lost its measles-free status because the PAHO found that the same strain of the virus had been spreading in the country for 12 months or more. Mexico and Bolivia lost their status on the same day as the US.

The US has had more than 5,400 cases in 2026 (at time of writing), more than twice as many as in all of 2025, and about 19 times as many as in 2024. Nearly everyone who got sick with measles was unvaccinated or had an unknown vaccination status.

In August 2026, when US President Donald Trump signed an executive order on new vaccination recommendations for children, it came at a time, when, as we reported, experts said people had stopped getting vaccinated against measles because infection rates were low. As PAHO's Jarbas Barbosa says above, avoiding vaccination when infection rates are low is a mistake.

To be fair, Trump's executive order listed the measles vaccine in a top category of vaccinations recommended for every child. But the administration's stance on vaccination in general is unclear; Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has often declared opposition to vaccination, including against measles, advising people to take vitamin A instead. In Texas, this led to children being hospitalized with toxic levels of the supplement, and left them with no protection against measles.

Before the COVID-19 pandemic, 95% of US kindergartners had their measles shots. Now, it's 92%, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Protection (CDC). That leaves about 280,000 kindergartners unprotected.
In the Texas counties, where a 2025 measles outbreak began, coverage was as low as 77% at the time.

US children usually need vaccines to start school, but most states let parents opt out for religious or personal reasons, with no doctor involved. In 24 states, so many children were exempt that those states couldn't reach the 95% threshold even if every other child got vaccinated.

But vaccination rates have fallen elsewhere in the world as well, including in Europe. In Germany, where measles infections have also risen, experts blame anti-vaccination rhetoric that emerged during the COVID-19 pandemic.
The 95% measles vaccination rule explained
It all comes down to math.

A person sick with measles can infect up to18 other, unprotected people. With vaccination, it is possible to increase the number of protected people and lower the number of people the sick person can infect.
To prevent a measles outbreak, a community needs about 95% of people to be vaccinated and/or immune. The vaccination consists of two doses of the MMR (measles, mumps, rubella) vaccine.

But even after the two doses, a person can expect to have only 97% protection against measles — 3% short of full protection — so, nearly everyone in the community has to be vaccinated to keep the average level of protect as close to 100% as possible.

"For some diseases like measles, even a small decrease in vaccination rates can lead to more outbreaks of disease [so] community immunity requires over 95% of susceptible individuals to be immunized," says Andrew Racine, president of the American Academy of Pediatrics.

And the 95% has to hold everywhere. A good national average can be affected by, for example, a single school where only 70% of the children are vaccinated. And that is where the outbreak start is likely to start.
In the US, where vaccination rates at kindergartens have dropped to 92%, that small difference is big enough to cause a measles outbreak.
The picture is mixed worldwide
Around the world, measles deaths have dropped by 88% since 2000, thanks to vaccines.
But progress has stalled. Only about three out of four children worldwide get both doses of the vaccine. The biggest outbreaks right now are in Bangladesh, Indonesia and Guatemala.
Data from Europe shows that things can get better. In the European Union, cases fell from more than 35,000 in 2024 to about 2,300 the following year, with no measles-related deaths.
Romania went from more than 30,000 cases in 2024 to about 4,200 in 2025.
Hungary, where 99% of children are vaccinated, there have been no measles cases in the past year.
But in January, six European countries lost their measles-free status, including the UK, Spain and Austria. Across Europe, eight out of ten people who got measles in 2025 were unvaccinated.

The Americas are seeing a major surge in measles infections, with more than 58,000 cases in 2026, over four times as many as this time (November) in 2025. Guatemala has been hit hardest, with almost 35,000 cases.

The deadliest outbreaks are in Africa. African Union countries have so far reported nearly 1,800 measles deaths in 2026, about 1,650 of them in Democratic Republic of Congo. Yet, Sudan, despite the war, raised first-dose measles coverage by 22 percentage points in 2025, which was the world's largest gain.
What you need to know about measles
Measles is extremely contagious. One person can infect up to 18 unprotected people, which makes it about 12 times more contagious than the flu.

The virus can linger in the air for up to two hours after a sick person has left the room. And people spread it before they know they are sick. Someone with measles is contagious for four days before the rash appears and four days after.

It's not just a rash. About one in five unvaccinated people who get measles in the US ends up in the hospital. Measles can weaken the immune system for years, making it harder to fight off other infections.
But it's preventable. Two doses of the MMR vaccine (which also protects against mumps and rubella) protect 97% of people for life.

articles.title: Is Pakistan backing anti-Taliban groups in Afghanistan?
articles.summary: The Taliban rulers in Afghanistan have accused Pakistan of aiding and sheltering armed resistance groups. The allegations come amid heightened tensions and are likely to deepen the rift between the…

image.caption: Islamabad has repeatedly demanded that the Taliban take action against anti-Pakistan militant groups operating from Afghan soilImage: Abdul Basit/AFP

blocks.text: The Taliban authorities in Afghanistan claim that the Pakistani government is supporting armed Afghan groups that are opposed to their rule, an accusation Islamabaddenies.
Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi recently alleged that Pakistan had launched a "project to destabilize Afghanistan."
He claimed that "thousands of armed individuals have gathered along the Durand Line (Afghanistan-Pakistan border) to undermine the stability achieved in Afghanistan."
The accusations come after months of border clashes between Afghan Taliban and Pakistani forces.

In July, the Afghanistan Freedom Front (AFF), an anti-Taliban group, reportedly clashed with Taliban forces in the Zebak district of Badakhshan, a northeastern Afghan province. The group said it also carried out attacks in Nooristan and Kunar provinces in October.
Another "resistance group," the United Front of Afghanistan, claimed it attacked Taliban forces in Kandahar province along the border with Pakistan.

"The people who created insecurity in Badakhshan crossed from Chitral [in Pakistan] and later fled back to Chitral. They had been brought in. Even Pakistani military personnel were with them," alleged Zabihullah Mujahid, Taliban's main spokesperson, in an interview with DW's Pashto-Dari service in September.
Pakistan's Ministry of Information swiftly dismissed the allegations as propaganda.
Groups that oppose the Taliban rule in Afghanistan say they are not supported by any external force, and their resistance is purely indigenous.
How 5 years of Taliban rule have changed Afghanistan
Pakistan's 'leverage' amid tense ties
More than five years since returning to power in Kabul, the Taliban have consolidated their control over Afghanistan and largely suppressed both armed resistance groups and political dissidents.

Shinkai Karokhail, a former Afghan member of parliament, told DW it would be logistically difficult for anti-Taliban Afghan groups to cross the Pakistani border and enter Afghanistan without Islamabad's support, referring to clashes in Badakhshan and Nooristan provinces.
"It is simply impossible," she said.

The Taliban themselves maintained close ties with Pakistan in the 1990s during their first stint in power. Some US officials even claimed that Islamabad didn't relinquish its support to the Islamist group even after September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks in the United States. Islamabad has always refuted these allegations.
But Afrasiab Khattak, a Pakistani political analyst and former senator, believes that Pakistani support for anti-Taliban groups is "real."
"Taliban opponents come to Islamabad, hold meetings, and it is a part of Pakistan's policy toward Afghanistan," he told DW.
Qandil Abbas, an associate professor of politics and international relations at Quaid-i-Azam University in Islamabad, disagrees.
"Pakistan may provide political support [to Taliban opponents], but not military support," she told DW.

Ali Ahmad Jalali, a professor at the Near East South Asia Center for Strategic Studies at the National Defense University in Washington DC, said it is possible that Islamabad is backing Taliban opponents as a "leverage."

"When such incidents take place along the Afghanistan-Pakistan border, and given Pakistan's history of support for Afghan groups, it would not be surprising if Pakistan is supporting these groups," Jalali said.
Are Pakistan and Afghanistan heading for war?
Islamabad accuses Taliban of similar tactics

Pakistani officials have repeatedly demanded that the Taliban take action against anti-Pakistan militant groups, particularly the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), a militant group responsible for attacking Pakistani civilians and soldiers, and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), an outlawed armed separatist group active in its western Balochistan province.
Islamabad alleges that these groups organize and launch attacks inside Pakistan from Afghan territory with Taliban support.

"Meaningful progress requires Afghan authorities to address legitimate security concerns of neighboring countries, particularly the threat of terrorism," Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said this week at the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) summit in Islamabad.
Islamabad said on Friday that Afghanistan was not invited to participate in the ECO gathering as Pakistan does not recognize the Taliban regime in Kabul.
Analyst Jalali, who served as Afghanistan's interior minister from 2003 to 2005, argues that Islamabad is demanding something the Taliban may neither be willing nor able to provide.

"Pakistan wants the Taliban to cooperate in fighting against groups such as the TTP. But the TTP has long fought alongside the Afghan Taliban. There are ideological as well as friendly ties between the two. They seek a similar political system, and some Afghan Taliban members may even be among TTP fighters," he added.
Analysts also point to the Taliban's efforts to strengthen relations with India, Pakistan's long-standing regional rival, as a cause of concern for Islamabad.

Malek Sitez, Afghan expert and researcher of international relations, argues that Pakistan, among other things, doesn't want Kabul to be close to New Delhi. But Pakistan no longer has the kind of influence over Afghanistan that it had in the past, he said.
Under Taliban shadow, Afghans in Pakistan look to Germany
Is Pakistan seeking to remove the Taliban from power?
Despite these accusations and counteraccusations from both sides, Jalali believes Pakistan still does not seek to remove the Taliban from power.

"I do not think Pakistan can or wants to overthrow the Taliban and replace them with another group," he underlined. Instead, he stressed, Islamabad's objective is to pressure the Taliban into cooperating against the TTP.

Aziz Barez, a political analyst of Afghanistan and regional affairs, is of the view that Afghan groups opposed to the Taliban can also not fully trust Islamabad, adding that they may welcome alleged Pakistani support but are also aware that such backing could be temporary.
"It is possible that Pakistan and the Taliban will resolve their differences tomorrow and become close allies again," he told DW.
Ahmad Waheed Ahmady and Helay Asad contributed to this report.

articles.title: COP31 climate talks spill into overtime as nations quarrel over fossil fuels
articles.summary: The draft also drops mention of a $120 billion target for finance to help developing countries adapt to climate change

blocks.text: SHAME. Activists unsatisfied with the second draft text at COP31 hold a silent protest outside the plenary hall, where delegates meet at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, on November 20, 2026.
Umit Bektas/Reuters
The draft also drops mention of a $120 billion target for finance to help developing countries adapt to climate change

items: The COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, is facing significant challenges as negotiators from nearly 200 countries struggle to reach an agreement on fossil fuels and climate finance, with environmental groups criticizing the lack of ambition.

Key points of contention include the omission of fossil fuel references in the draft agreement and the removal of a $120 billion financial target for developing countries, leading to concerns about the effectiveness of the negotiations.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

ANTALYA, Turkey – The COP31 climate conference slipped into overtime on Friday, November 20, as negotiators from nearly 200 countries struggled to bridge deep divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance.

Environmental groups tracking the two-week conference heaped pressure on host Turkey and lead negotiator Australia, saying the meeting was on track to be the “worst COP ever” because it lacked ambition to address the worsening climate crisis.

The biggest points of tension center around whether a final deal should mention the fossil fuels that are the primary driver of global warming, and whether it should address financial support to help poorer countries adjust.

Climate negotiators stripped out all references to ending the use of fossil fuels in a slimmed-down draft agreement published on Thursday, November 19, following objections from Saudi Arabia and other major oil and gas producers.

“It is not acceptable to have a COP or a cover document that does not even mention fossil fuels, and we simply will not put up with it,” Panamanian Environment Minister Juan Carlos Navarro told a press conference.
The draft also dropped mention of a $120 billion target for finance to help developing countries adapt to climate change.
A new version was expected later on Friday, but hopes of major changes in tone were not high.

“We can see where it’s going, and it’s not going to be a high-ambition text,” said Ralph Regenvanu, climate minister of the South Pacific island nation of Vanuatu, which is threatened by sea level rise and worsening storms.
The Australian president of negotiations, Chris Bowen, told reporters he remained hopeful of a deal everyone could get behind.
“Things worth doing, in my experience, don’t come easy,” he said. “People have strong views, of course. I’m not stepping away from that, but no one has said to me ‘Let’s give up and go home’.”
While the conference was scheduled to end on Friday, in recent years efforts to secure consensus at climate summits have regularly blown past this deadline by more than 24 hours.
This year’s talks have been further complicated by war and rising living costs, which are competing for the attention of policymakers and the public.

The United States, the world’s largest historical greenhouse gas emitter, is also absent from the talks for the second year in a row after President Donald Trump ended cooperation on the climate, calling global warming a hoax.

A UN report last month found the world is set to exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) of warming above pre-industrial levels, a threshold that governments agreed under the 2015 Paris Agreement to pursue efforts to respect.

The draft deal now under discussion acknowledges the projected overshoot and encourages accelerated deployment of technologies that can remove greenhouse gases from the atmosphere to help eventually bring temperatures back down.

But several country delegations have criticised the mention of carbon removal in the draft, saying the technologies are expensive and unproven at scale, and that including them in a deal opens the door to continued oil and gas development.

“It allows developed countries to continue producing oil and gas with a claim that CCUS (carbon capture, utilisation and storage) will fix it, while we will have a bigger role to triple renewables, which is not balanced at all,” said Bob Natifu, Uganda’s commissioner of climate change and carbon markets.
OPEC members Saudi Arabia and Venezuela have both made a case for a future role for fossil fuels in their official speeches to the conference.
Mohamed Adow, director of the climate think tank Power Shift Africa, was downbeat:
“The COP presidents want to tell us this has been a great COP. Well, I can tell you without any doubt that this has been the worst COP ever.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Germany face belgium in Nations League quarterfinals — Klopp plays down favorites tag
articles.summary: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is looking to "carry positive momentum forward" as his team draw neighboring Belgium in the quarterfinals of the UEFA Nations League.

image.caption: Based on their FIFA rankings, the Germany-Belgium matchup should produce a closely contested tieImage: Peter Schatz/picture alliance

blocks.text: Germany, who finished top of Group A2 following their 5-0 win over the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday are to face Belgium in the Nations League quarterfinals—after they finished second in Group A1. The Belgians recently came up with a statement result of their own, beating Italy 4-1. The match-up between the neighboring countries promises to be closely contested, with Belgium sitting at No. 8 in the men's rankings, three places above Germany.

The head coach of Belgium is former Bayern Munich player Mark van Bommel, who took over from Rudi Garcia following the World Cup, where they were knocked out by eventual champions Spain in the quarterfinals.

Germany head into the knockout phase on a high note, not only because they won their group, but also the way they performed in their last two matches, against Serbia and the Netherlands in the group stage.
Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp followed the draw, held in Nyon on Friday, from the German FA's (DFB) Frankfurt offices. He played down the notion that Germany enter the tie as the favorites.
"I've practically never given it any thought. It's never interested me," he said.

"An awful lot can happen in that time. We're very happy with the final impression we left, yet we're also fully aware that we're only at the very beginning of a development process. We want to carry this positive momentum forward—there's still a great deal to be done."
Historical success for Germany against Belgium
The matches are slated for March 25 and March 30, 2027, and having won their group, Germany will have home-field advantage for the second leg.
Germany and Belgium have faced each other 26 times to date, with West Germany and Germany having the upper hand with 20 wins, five defeats and one draw.
Should Germany advance to the semifinals, they will go on to face the winner of England and Norway – a World Cup quarterfinals rematch.
In the other two semifinals matchups, the Netherlands drew Portugal, while the top pairing sees Spain face France in a rematch of one of last summer's World Cup semifinals.
The "Final Four" mini tournament is to be held from June 9 to 13 but the host venue won't be determined until the semifinal lineup has been completed.

articles.title: Marcos rejects call to reassess economic team amid 'malaise'
articles.summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Friday stood by his current economic team even as he was urged by a senator to take a closer look at his Cabinet amid a so-called “economic malaise.”

blocks.text: Published November 20, 2026 10:44pm
President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Friday stood by his current economic team even as he was urged by a senator to take a closer look at his Cabinet amid a so-called “economic malaise.”

In a Kapihan with the media in Shenzhen, China, the President said he disagrees with the call of Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson, who earlier raised concerns about the dipping Philippine stocks, the weakening peso, and rising inflation, among other issues.
“No, I don’t…I disagree with him. I’m sorry, but I disagree with him,” Marcos said.
“All the difficulties we’re going under can be clearly directly traced to the war in Iran,” he added.
Cabinet revamp
Marcos likewise addressed speculations about recent changes in his Cabinet, saying that he is only trying to “put the best people to the best use” amid developments worldwide.
“Everything was done for a particular reason. There’s no general reason that I’m not happy with the Cabinet or anything like that. No, not at all. Quite the contrary,” he said.
“Issues come up that didn’t exist before in certain departments. So we’re trying to put the people who are best able to address those issues into the proper department,” he added.
The President said that the reshuffle also had something to do with his administration’s plans.
“[We’re] trying to get the best people into whatever position we need to best be able to push our priorities for the future,” he said.
Marcos also stood firm that shifting one Cabinet member to another position does not produce instability in the government.

“The job of a Cabinet secretary does not remain exactly the same from day one until day whatever it is six years later. Nagbabago talaga ‘yan (it really changes). And then we make our own plans as we go along,” he said.

“And then we have to worry about shocks like the war in Iran, so we have to adjust also to that. And then now with AI coming up, we have to adjust also to that. And then the different developments in geopolitics, we also have to adjust to that,” he added. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Defense witness can’t explain discrepancy in Cale88 sales, cash inflow
articles.summary: DTI Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo's testimony on Cale88 raises more suspicions about the banana chips exporter's inward remittances from China

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – A defense witness for Vice President Sara Duterte on Friday, November 20, admitted he could not explain the discrepancy between the cash inflows and declared sales revenues of Cale88 Foods Corporation, a company being linked to the Vice President.

On Day 45 of the impeachment trial, the defense presented Ceferino Rodolfo, Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) undersecretary for industry development and investment promotions, to establish the legitimacy of Cale88.

Rodolfo testified that Cale88 is registered as an export enterprise under the DTI-Board of Investments (BOI) and has complied with the agency’s registration requirements. He also identified the company as a micro, small, and medium enterprise (MSME).

In his interjection, Senator-judge Sherwin Gatchalian questioned the huge disparity between Cale88’s declared sales and its reported cash inflows, asking Rodolfo to explain the possible reasons behind the discrepancy.

“In relation to the operations of the company and the documents they submitted to us, we don’t see any reason for the inward remittances to exceed the declared sales revenue submitted to us,” Rodolfo said.

Rodolfo later admitted that it was his first time encountering such a discrepancy involving a company. He stressed, however, that he was not qualified to explain the figures, saying Cale88’s president, treasurer, operating officer, and export sales manager would be in a better position to do so.

Cale88, a banana chips production company partly owned by Duterte’s husband, Manases Carpio, came under scrutiny during the impeachment trial after Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) records showed that it received P776 million in cash inflows despite having only P125,000 in paid-up capital and declaring P208 million in sales.

Lawyer Alex Cabrera, who prepared a forensic financial report on Duterte’s bank and financial records, described Cale88’s business model as “implausible.” He likened its operations to a “revolving door,” which he said was a symptom of money laundering.
Senator-judge Panfilo “Ping” Lacson said the central issue was not Cale88’s legitimacy as a registered company but allegations that it may have been used as a front for money laundering.
“What we want to see is proof or records – waybills, shipping records,” Lacson said.

“I know you said earlier that those are with the Customs, but we are all wondering, at least, if the defense could refute the forensic financial analysis, and erase our doubts that Cale88 might have been used,” he added.
Defense counsel Michael Poa clarified that Rodolfo’s testimony was only preliminary, assuring senator-judges that the defense would present other witnesses to address the allegations.
“We understand what you are looking for. We have witnesses for that,” Poa said.

Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros said on October 6 that an investigation by her office showed that Cale88 Food Corporation received remittances from Chinese companies, including entities linked to China’s state-owned sector.

Prior to that, Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura told the impeachment court that Cale88 received P319 million from China and Hong Kong, based on covered transaction reports (CTRs) and suspicious transaction reports (STRs).
The National Security Council (NSC) responded to these disclosures last October by saying it would look into the reported inflow of Chinese funds to Cale88.

Vice President Duterte has generally been silent and uncritical about China’s harassment of Philippine vessels in the West Philippine Sea, which critics say could be linked to her family’s business ties with Chinese companies.

Im a related development, the Senate impeachment court has set a new schedule for the trial as it takes a brief break to give way for the Senate plenary deliberations on the proposed 2027 national budget.

Impeachment Court Presiding Officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero initially announced that the trial would resume on Thursday, November 26, reverting to its original schedule of 10 am to 2 pm. However, lead defense counsel Sheila Sison asked for the indulgence of the court, saying their witnesses are unavailable on November 26 and November 27.

“We would like to be candid to the court and say that our next witnesses are not available on November 26 and 27. Also given that we are only informed today that there will be hearings for next week and as you know, this is not our only commitment and we had also made commitments to our other engagements,” Sison said.

“We are not interested in a protracted, prolonged trial of this case and as this court has seen, the defense has been prudent with the time of this court, has not abused this court, and has not wasted three months time presenting witnesses that will eventually be withdrawn,” she said.
House prosecutor Terry Ridon asked for Sison’s remarks to be stricken from the records. He also called for consequences to be placed on the defense for lessening the days of presentation.
Escudero said he would take under advisement Ridon’s manifestation. He also said the impeachment proceedings will resume next month with the following schedule:
December 1 to 4: 10 am – 3 pm
December 14 to 17 (if necessary)
